result.pool: Disasters & Famine: granary, NO medical provision
result.summary: This pool table contains three spines and NOT ONE FACE. I confirmed against a sibling table (Disasters_Famine_NO_reserves_NO_medical_provision.md) that face rows are rendered when they exist, so either this block was written spine-only or the faces never reached the table; the chair must settle that before reading the counts below as coverage, because this audit is over three lines, not over a pool. On those three lines the cut is honest and inside the claim freeze. No claim moved, no speaker was deleted (the spines carry none by design, the engine's bare voice under ruling 40), and the implementer correctly killed the two mechanical bars live at HEAD: the semicolon in variant 1 and the two occurrences of "will" in variant 2. Variant 3 is a genuine 42b sharpening, from "knows which of the two it fears" to "It is the sick year the town fears", and must go on the 42b list because the old refutation does not cover it. The cut was, however, MECHANICAL RATHER THAN TO THE STANDARD on variants 1 and 2: in variant 1 the semicolon became a full stop but the clause after it is still a consequence the first sentence already entails, which converts a 42 breach into a 42a breach rather than curing it; in variant 2 the trailing "and the town has built nothing that would" still restates "Nothing here carries it through a plague" from the builder's side. Both are SHOULD_FIX with concrete replacements. Before the cut none of the three lines passed the owner's standard; after it, one does.

findings.was: The town can outlast a hungry year at {settlement} and has no answer at all to a sick one, and knows which of the two it fears.
findings.now: The town can outlast a hungry year at {settlement} and has no answer at all to a sick one. It is the sick year the town fears.
findings.why: The old tail "knows which of the two it fears" names no fear and so makes no claim a reader can act on, the textbook 42b failure. The new line commits to one reading. This is lawful and required, but it is NOT covered by the old refutation and must be collected for refuting: in particular the refuter has to check whether the card supports attributing a fear to the town as a body at all, rather than only the two capability facts.
findings.readingChosen: The sick year, not the hungry one. The pool's own state is granary present, NO medical provision: the grain store makes a failed harvest survivable and there is no provision of any kind against disease, so of the two years named in the same sentence only the sick one is uncovered. The alternative reading would contradict the first half of its own sentence.

findings.was: {settlement} can feed itself through a failed harvest and has nothing at all against disease; a sickness here spreads until it stops of its own accord.
findings.now: {settlement} can feed itself through a failed harvest and has nothing at all against disease. A sickness here spreads until it stops of its own accord.
findings.why: The only change is semicolon to full stop. That clears the mechanical bar but leaves the offence: apply the 42a test and delete "A sickness here spreads until it stops of its own accord." The first sentence is missing no fact, because "has nothing at all against disease" already entails that nothing stops a sickness, so the second sentence only tells the reader what to make of the first. Under 42 it was a trailing explanatory clause; under 42a it is now a trailing explanatory sentence.
findings.proposedFix: {settlement} can feed itself through a failed harvest and has nothing at all against disease.

findings.was: The stores will carry the town through hunger. Nothing here will carry it through a plague, and the town has not built anything that would.
findings.now: The stores carry the town through hunger. Nothing here carries it through a plague, and the town has built nothing that would.
findings.why: The two "will" bars are correctly gone and "has built nothing" is a better shape than "has not built anything", but the trailing clause survives untouched and is the same fact twice: "Nothing here carries it through a plague" and "the town has built nothing that would" are one absence stated from the capability side and then from the builder's side. A qualifier belongs inside the sentence; this clause adds no fact, it explains the one before it.
findings.proposedFix: The stores carry the town through hunger. The town has built nothing that would carry it through a plague.

findings.now: spines changed 3 of 3 · faces changed 0 · faces unchanged 0
findings.why: The table carries no face rows at all, where every sibling table in the same directory carries five to fifteen. Either this block was written spine-only, or the faces were lost between the pool and the table, in which case this audit has checked three lines out of a pool that may hold twenty and the "faces changed 0" header is reassuring for the wrong reason. The chair should confirm against the face-count register, which the brief says must not move, before treating this pool as audited.

All three variants run the identical figure, copes with hunger, no answer to sickness, then a tail that comments on the pair, so the four-variants rule buys register difference ([ledger], [unfolding], [street]) but not shape difference. The claim freeze rightly stopped the implementer from restructuring, so this is not a fault in the cut; it is a note for whoever next holds these three lines without the freeze on.

leastSure: "The stores carry the town through hunger." - the de-will fix turns a prediction into a habitual capability, and the audit brief counts a tense change as a moved claim; I read it as inside the freeze because "will" is a hard mechanical bar and present-generic is the only lawful way out, with the underlying fact (the store is sufficient against a failed harvest) untouched.

"It is the sick year the town fears." - I let the second sentence stand under 42a on the grounds that a town's disposition is a fact and not strictly entailed by its provisions (a town can be complacent about plague), but it sits close to the line where the reader was going to infer it anyway.

"A sickness here spreads until it stops of its own accord." - I call it entailed and cuttable, but a reading exists on which it adds something the first sentence does not say, namely that nobody intervenes even informally; if the refuter takes that reading the line earns its place and my proposed fix loses a fact.
